paragraphs.title: No-amon as an Example of a Fallen Fortified City

answers: No-amon
Jerusalem
Babylon
easy.explanation: The passage asks, “Art thou better than populous No?”
easy.q: Which city is mentioned as an example of a fall?

answers: Walls of fire
Waters and rivers
Snow-covered mountains
easy.explanation: No-amon was situated among rivers and had waters round about it.

answers: It was carried away into captivity
It conquered other cities
It became stronger
easy.explanation: The passage says that No-amon “went into captivity.”

answers: Water, strength, and allied helpers
No walls and no defenders
A location in a desert without enemies
medium.explanation: No-amon had surrounding waters, the strength of Ethiopia and Egypt, and help from Put and Lubim.
medium.q: What advantages did No-amon have according to the passage?

answers: To show that the city had no inhabitants
To show that much support still could not prevent its fall
To prove that those nations defeated Nineveh
medium.explanation: Even with powerful allies and defenses, No-amon was carried away captive.
medium.q: Why are the nations that helped No-amon mentioned?

answers: It was taken away as a captive
It went to a place of celebration
It entered the city gate
medium.explanation: The phrase means that the people were conquered and taken away by their enemies.

Both defeated all their enemies

challenge.q: What comparison is implied between No-amon and Nineveh?

answers: It shows that the defeat was widespread and severe
It describes the city’s prosperity
It proves that the children defended the city

challenge.q: Why is it important that the young children of No-amon were also affected?

answers: Allies do not guarantee deliverance
Allies can never be defeated
No-amon was not a fortified city

Springs of water

answers: They will be firmly shut

They will disappear under water

They will grow after the war
